knowledge_point.title: Solving for Two Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-13 \\ 17 \\ -29\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-13 \\ 17 \\ -29\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-13 \\ 17 \\ -29\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-13 \\ 17 \\ -29\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-13 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=17 \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=-29\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $2$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} &=-9\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=-9$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=17 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3(-9) &=17 \\ -2{x}_{1} &=-10 \\ {x}_{1} &=5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=5$ and ${x}_{2}=-9$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=-29 \\ 3(5)+5(-9) &=-29 \\ -30 &=-29\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

$$

$$

which gives a true statement.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ -2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-8{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2} &=-14 \\ -{x}_{2} &=-4 \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the second equation we get ${x}_{2}=4$.

Substituting ${x}_{2}=4$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2} &=-14 \\ 3{x}_{1}-8(4) &=-14 \\ 3{x}_{1} &=18 \\ {x}_{1} &=6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=6$ and ${x}_{2}=4$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=4 \\ -2(6)+4(4) &=4 \\ 4 &=4\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=6$ and ${x}_{2}=4$, which means

$$
6{a}_{1}+4{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(6)+(4)=10.
$$
